hints: Focus on who attacks whom in nucleophilic addition, a nucleophile with a lone pair seeks the delta positive carbon of the polar C=O bond.
Identify the real nucleophile here, in cyanide ion the lone pair and negative charge that does the attacking is on carbon, not nitrogen, to give $^{-}\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$.
Check the curly arrows carefully, one must start at the lone pair on C of $\text{CN}^{-}$ and point to the carbonyl C, and the other must start at the C=O bond and point onto O.
walkthrough:
**Spot the electrophile in propanone**

Propanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. Oxygen is more electronegative than carbon, so the bond is polarised as $\text{C}^{\delta+}=\text{O}^{\delta-}$.

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^{\delta+}(=\text{O}^{\delta-})-\text{CH}_3$$
The carbonyl carbon is electron poor and will be attacked by a nucleophile.

**Spot the nucleophile in cyanide**

Cyanide ion is best drawn as $\text{N}\equiv\text{C}^{-}$ with a lone pair on carbon. It is the carbon end that attacks.

$$^{-}:\text{C}\equiv\text{N}:$$
So any diagram showing $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}^{-}$ attacking through nitrogen is wrong.

**Apply the curly arrow rules**

A curly arrow shows movement of a pair of electrons from electron rich to electron poor.

$$\text{lone pair on } \text{C of CN}^{-} \rightarrow \text{C}^{\delta+} \text{ and } \text{C=O} \rightarrow \text{O}^{\delta-}$$
Arrow 1 must start at the lone pair on the C of $\text{CN}^{-}$ and point to the carbonyl C. Arrow 2 must start at the C=O double bond and point onto O to give an alkoxide intermediate.

**Select the correct diagram**

Only one diagram has C attacking (not N), the first arrow pointing from $\text{CN}^{-}$ to the carbonyl C (not backwards), and the second arrow pointing from the double bond onto O.
That combination gives the first stage intermediate $\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{C(CN)O}^{-}$.

options.A: Incorrect. The main arrow is drawn backwards, pointing from the carbonyl carbon toward the cyanide ion. That would imply electrons flow from the electrophile to the nucleophile, which is opposite to nucleophilic attack.
options.B: Incorrect. Although the cyanide is shown with the correct C end, the main curly arrow points the wrong way, from the carbonyl toward cyanide. A nucleophile must donate to the electrophile, not the reverse.
options.C: Incorrect. The arrow direction toward the carbonyl C is sensible, but the ion is drawn as $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}^{-}$ with nitrogen attacking. In $\text{CN}^{-}$ the donor lone pair is on carbon, so attack must be by C to form a C-C bond, not by N.
options.D: Correct. The ion is $\text{N}\equiv\text{C}^{-}$ with the lone pair on carbon, the curly arrow starts at that lone pair and points to the $\text{C}^{\delta+}$ of propanone, and the second curly arrow moves the C=O electrons onto $\text{O}^{\delta-}$. This correctly shows formation of the new C-C bond and the alkoxide ion.
